learning_outcomes.text: Ability to identify the main problems and challenges of our society and propose, design and develop sustainable, innovative, and participatory methodologies and/or technologies to improve people's lives, making responsible use of resources and knowing how to determine the impact that different projects have on the economy, society, or the environment.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

syllabus_topics: Block I: Primary manufacturing technologies. Topic 1: Powder processing techniques for ceramics and metals.
Topic 2. Manufacturing processes used in polymers.
Topic 3: Manufacturing processes used in composites.
Block II: Secondary operations. Topic 4: Surface engineering.
Block III: Advanced machining technologies. Topic 6: Non-conventional machining technologies.
assessment_rules: The general evaluation model is continuous assessment, where no individual activity can exceed 60% of the global grade. Non-re-evaluable activities should not exceed 40% of the global grade and typically have no minimum pass mark, except for practical activities that cannot be reproduced. Students failing or not attending the ordinary exam can re-sit only the re-evaluable activities. A minimum grade of 4.5 is required for written tests (PE1, PE2) and 5.0 for laboratory practices (SE3), with attendance to lab sessions being mandatory.
